Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(5,-5\sqrt{3})$, find the polar equation of the ray.
worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-5\sqrt{3}}{5}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we find the angle in the fourth quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$
